forcedChoices.reason: The text speaks to the readers; plural form per the Spanish rules.
Spanish forces a gender for "child"; the English uses "he" for the child elsewhere in the section.
Spanish "conciencia" covers both conscience and consciousness; "moral" keeps "conscience" apart.
"eventuates" is used in its plain sense here, not the technical sense of the glossary form "eventuar".
"actual virtue" is plain "real", not the philosophic "en acto".
Spanish "su" is ambiguous (his/your); the generic "your" becomes "propia" with the emphasis kept.
"spiritism" here is a philosophic system opposite materialism; "espiritismo" is the glossary form for séance spiritualism.
"actuality" paired with "potentials" takes the philosophic glossary sense.
"godless" with no capital keeps open whether a God or gods came in.
